clue.text: Habits of the male baboon

parts.note: a male is a man
habits are routines, and a drill is a fixed routine practised until it becomes habit

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes the customary behaviour of a male baboon.
explanation.walkthrough: The drill is itself a baboon-like monkey, which adds a wink to the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African primate closely related to the baboons and often classed among them.

clue.text: Get a role adapted for second personality

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered and rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An actor is told to get a part reworked to play a second character.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'other self', the phrase names a person's distinct alternative persona.

clue.text: Intensity of French substance I ignored

parts.note: de is the French word for 'of'

indicators.note: ignored means the letter I is left out of the word for substance

parts.note: the pith of something is its substance or core

explanation.surface: Someone notes the intensity of French substance while I am overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of feeling or colour is its intensity or profundity.

clue.text: More or less popular time on course with analgesics

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be in
a round of golf is the time spent going round the course
painkillers numb you, so jokingly they are numbers (things that numb)

explanation.surface: A golfer's popular time on the course is spent taking painkillers.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBERS here is read as 'things that numb', not figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving figures approximately, rounded off, is speaking roughly or approximately.

clue.text: Don't change holiday bookings even at the outset

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday

indicators.note: at the outset means only the opening letters of the two preceding words are used

explanation.surface: A travel agent advises not altering holiday bookings, even from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something alone is to let it stay as it is, not altering it.

clue.text: Quantity of dirt suddenly swirling?

indicators.note: swirling means turning round, so the letters taken are read backwards
a quantity of the words means just a portion of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A puff of dirt whips up suddenly in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters TSUD sit inside 'dirt suddenly'; 'swirling' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine particles of dirt whirling in the air is exactly what is meant by a cloud of powdery grime.

clue.text: Silent instrument? Bam! I pound madly

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist bangs away madly at a keyboard that makes no noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb piano is a soundless keyboard used for finger practice, mute in both senses.

clue.text: End of day fixed: around noon in America

indicators.note: around means the word for fixed surrounds the other letters

parts.note: something fixed is set

indicators.note: in means the letter for noon goes inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A deadline is fixed for the end of the day, around noon American time.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun going down marks the close of the day, the evening.

clue.text: Psychological trauma: I'd misjudged its sincerity

indicators.note: misjudged means got wrong, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A patient confesses to misjudging someone's sincerity and suffering trauma as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainty about who one is, a recognised state of psychological turmoil.

clue.text: Endless commotion about high, drugged state

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the other letters
endless means the final letter of the word for commotion is dropped

parts.note: a storm is an uproar or commotion
up means high

explanation.surface: A constant uproar surrounds someone high and drugged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed near-unconscious condition, often induced by narcotics.

clue.text: Poor prognosis one brought forward for stomach

indicators.note: brought forward means the letter for one moves nearer the front of the phrase

parts.note: a poor prognosis is a bad omen
A means one, as in 'a single'

explanation.surface: A doctor brings forward a gloomy prognosis about someone's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly region, containing the digestive organs, is the stomach area in everyday speech.

clue.text: Annoying type keeping you in highbrow cinema?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for an annoying person goes round the other

parts.note: an arse is British slang for an irritating person
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An irritating person keeps you inside an intellectual film theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An art house is a cinema showing serious, artistic films, hence highbrow.

clue.text: New Zealand coastal city, one investing in new wharf

indicators.note: investing in means going into, so the letter for one is placed inside

parts.note: a pier is a wharf or landing stage
A means one, as in 'a single'

explanation.surface: A New Zealand port is described with someone investing in its new wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: Napier is a seaside city in Hawke's Bay on the North Island.

clue.text: Shakespearean take on the virtue seen amongst criminals?

definitions.text: Shakespearean take on the virtue seen amongst criminals?

parts.words: Shakespearean take on the virtue seen amongst criminals?
parts.note: a quotation from The Merchant of Venice about how one kind act shines brightly in a wicked setting, like a good turn among crooks

explanation.walkthrough: Portia says 'So shines a good deed in a naughty world'; the clue reads that wicked world as a criminal underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation describes virtue standing out against wickedness, as a kindness would among crooks.

clue.text: Old points about regulations abandoned by university and no longer claimed

indicators.note: about means the compass letters surround the shortened word

parts.note: the compass points west, north, east and south give W, N, E and S

indicators.note: abandoned by means the university letter is dropped from the word for regulations

parts.note: rules are regulations

explanation.surface: Old points about regulations are abandoned by a university and nobody claims them any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that belongs to nobody, no owner asserting a right to it, is unclaimed.

clue.text: Insect tucking into prairie fruit

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the insect sits within the word for prairie

parts.note: a prairie is a grassy plain
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect eats its way into fruit on the prairie.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit eaten cooked.

clue.text: See 13
Doctor discharging English poet

indicators.note: discharging means letting go, so the letter for English is removed

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain

explanation.surface: A doctor discharges an English poet from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a houseman is a newly qualified doctor working in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman wrote the verse collection A Shropshire Lad.

clue.text: Put an end to booze

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to stop it
whisky from Scotland, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to stop drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means to quash something; the other is the whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Beetle: repelled tailless one infesting watering-holes

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
infesting means getting into, so the shortened word goes inside the word for watering-holes

parts.note: bars are drinking places, watering-holes

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word for one is cut off

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A beetle infesting pubs is driven out, one without its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: An ace counts as one in cards and dice; 'repelled' reverses the whole assembled run, not just the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: United saying positive things, dismissing a rebellion

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter A is removed

parts.note: praising is saying positive things

explanation.surface: United fans praise their team but dismiss a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular revolt against authority is a rising up by the people.

clue.text: One in bed's sitting up, tolerating discomfort

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the reversed word
sitting up, in a down entry, means the letters are written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a cot is a bed, and the possessive adds S
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A patient sits up in bed, putting up with discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stoic bears pain without complaint, enduring hardship calmly.

clue.text: Article with more convoluted hypothesis

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A paper presents a more complicated hypothesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition put forward to be demonstrated by reasoning, a formal hypothesis in mathematics.

clue.text: Call to arms: "Hard work leads to added notoriety"

parts.note: a slog is hard work

indicators.note: leads means the opening letters of the following two words are taken

explanation.surface: A rallying cry claims hard work brings extra fame.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant a Gaelic war cry, a shout rallying people to battle.

clue.text: Politician avoiding defeats in such a way

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping out, so the politician's letters are dropped

parts.note: thumps means beats soundly, defeats
MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician manages to avoid defeats in some particular way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this manner, so, in the fashion described.

clue.text: Part of rocket, one shaped to receive most of support

indicators.note: to receive means the rearranged letters take the shortened word inside
shaped means formed anew, so the letters of the word are rearranged
most of means the last letter of the word for support is dropped

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: A rocket component is shaped to receive most of its supporting structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' turns ONE into NOE, which receives SECON (SECOND less its last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed front section of a rocket or missile, its streamlined tip.
